title: iwe-aewf-television
label: Rune

won.source: the federation's own comeback broadcast, "Back From the Dead," 28 June 2003

how: Pinned the defending champion King Snake, surviving two kickouts of the Snake Bite, in a career-vs-title stipulation match.

title: iwe-aewf-television
label: King Snake

won.source: The promotion's own billing on "Back From the Dead," 28 June 2003, introducing King Snake as "the reigning and defending AeWF Television champion of the world."

lost.source: the federation's own comeback broadcast, "Back From the Dead," 28 June 2003

how: Billed as reigning champion entering the match; no document in the held record states how or when he won the title.

title: iwe-world-tag-team
label: Enemies of the State

won.source: the federation's own comeback broadcast, "Back From the Dead," 28 June 2003

how: Won a four-way elimination match, eliminating God's Justice and then Team Scrapyards; the deciding pinfall on Karma followed an unseen Atkins chairshot, with Jett cutting off Adams' save attempt.

title: iwe-world-tag-team
label: God's Justice

won.source: The promotion's own billing on "Back From the Dead," 28 June 2003, calling God's Justice "the former IWE Tag Champs" as they were eliminated.

how: Billed mid-match as the promotion's own former champions; no document in the held record states how or when they won the titles.
notes: The four-way match itself bills the titles as "newly reinstated," implying the belts sat vacant between this reign and the tournament that crowned Enemies of the State; recorded from the promotion's own repeated billing per the museum's standing practice.

title: iwe-intercontinental
label: The Outlaw

won.source: the federation's own comeback broadcast, "Back From the Dead," 28 June 2003

how: Won a two-out-of-three-falls match against Christopher Maxwell (formerly Marcus Slade) for the vacant title, two falls to one: a Cactus and Scorpion Deathmatch, then a Flaming Table Match loss, then a steel cage match won by climbing down to the floor.
notes: The title itself had been vacant for four years per the broadcast's own commentary; no prior holder is named in the held record.

title: iwe-world-heavyweight
label: Johnny Malibu

won.source: the federation's own comeback broadcast, "Back From the Dead," 28 June 2003

how: Pinned Dante Reid with the Glamour Bomb in a three-way match (also involving Brian Floyd) for the vacant title, after hired interference from Enemies of the State turned on Floyd, who had paid for it, as well as Reid.
notes: The title had been vacant since the promotion's own 1999 closure per the broadcast's own commentary, which declines to name the prior champion ("Names aren't necessary"). A wholly unrelated held federation's own wrestler biography independently attests an earlier reign for a wrestler named Chris Hopper, corroborated by this card's own flashback footage; that reign is not separately recorded here for lack of a held show document to anchor it (see the title's own notes).
